course.title: Machine Learning Systems on One Machine
course.tagline: Find where time and memory go on one machine, fix the largest cost first, and prove each speed-up kept its quality
course.description: Participants find out where time and memory go between raw data and a served prediction, and fix the largest cost first. For a fictional agritech company they profile a data pipeline and a training step, estimate memory from weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache, apply mixed precision, batching, quantisation and pruning, export a model to a portable runtime, and benchmark latency, throughput and quality with repeated runs and intervals. Labs run on a laptop CPU, with an optional free notebook GPU, and every speed-up must be measured and checked for loss of quality.
course.audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career developers who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and software engineers moving into AI work.
prerequisites: AE-202 Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals
Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
Reads a histogram and computes a percentile

Setup: a laptop with uv (any recent processor, 8 GB of memory), or Google Colab, where a free GPU runtime is optional. Nothing downloads a model: both models are in the repository. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Explain how compute, memory capacity and memory bandwidth limit training and inference, and identify which one binds for a described workload, given four workload descriptions with model size, batch size and hardware figures
outcomes.evidence: a worked estimate for each workload that matches the reference within a stated margin

outcomes.text: Measure where time goes in a data pipeline and a training step with profilers and timers, and remove the largest bottleneck, given a slow training script for the leaf-image model
outcomes.evidence: a before-and-after profile and a measured speed-up with the change explained

outcomes.text: Compute the memory needed for weights, activations, optimiser state and the key-value cache and check each estimate against measured peak memory, given a small vision model and a small language model at three batch sizes and context lengths
outcomes.evidence: an estimate table next to measured peaks, with each difference explained

outcomes.text: Apply mixed precision, batching and compilation and report their effect on speed, memory and accuracy, given the training and inference scripts and a fixed test set
outcomes.evidence: a results table with time per step, throughput, peak memory and accuracy for each setting

outcomes.text: Apply post-training quantisation and pruning, export the model to a portable runtime and compare size, latency and quality with the original, given the trained classifier, a small language model and a held-out evaluation set
outcomes.evidence: a comparison table of size, median and tail latency and quality loss with an interval

outcomes.text: Prepare a benchmark that controls warm-up, repetitions, batch size and input mix, and report percentiles with confidence intervals, given two model variants and a target laptop
outcomes.evidence: a benchmark script and report that another participant re-runs within 10% of the reported median

outcomes.text: Optimise a model and its serving path to meet a stated latency and memory budget on a target device while keeping quality within an agreed tolerance, given a budget set by the company for its farm-office laptops and a quality floor on the held-out set
outcomes.evidence: an optimisation log ordered by measured impact and a final benchmark that meets the budget or explains the gap

case_study.name: Nama Agritech
case_study.summary: Nama Agritech is a fictional farm-advisory company whose agents run two models on old farm-office laptops: Waraqa, a leaf-disease classifier trained on 20,000 synthetic leaf images in ten disease classes and four crops, and Hasad, a small language model the course trained to answer 2,000 synthetic Arabic farmer questions in Modern Standard Arabic, Gulf dialect and mixed Arabic and English. Participants measure, profile, estimate memory, compress, export and benchmark both against the budget Nama set for its laptops; all data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: an optimisation study and its defence
days.subtitle: Eight minutes of results, a live re-run, four minutes of questions

capstone.summary: An optimisation study on a model of the participant's choice, submitted as a public repository whose README reports the baseline profile, each change ordered by measured impact, and the final latency, memory and quality against a stated budget with intervals and the hardware used, followed by an eight-minute defence and four minutes of questions
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository whose README reports the baseline profile, each change ordered by measured impact, and the final latency, memory and quality against the stated budget with intervals and the hardware used; profiler outputs, benchmark logs and the commit history are in the repository. Then the eight-minute defence: the participant re-runs the benchmark live, predicts the effect of a change the assessor proposes and then measures it.
